subject: app-rdef
title: APP.RDEF. -----STF. ------SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-8 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan), first of two on book p250. (C)APP-RDEF (the concept of apparent redefinition) is crossed simultaneously with STF (source-transfer functionalism) AND SOC-RT (social reality) — the unusual dual-partner formation indicating Braxton holds three concepts in tension. STF sits at the upper-center between subject and the second partner. SOC-RT anchors the upper-right. CRTF-D (creative-dynamic) hangs on the right output. PROJ-CONT (projectional continuance) sits centrally below STF. AFTF (affinity-tendency functionalism) anchors the lower-center. ALT-F (alternative functionalism) and PR-TRS (principal transference) form the lower-right cluster. (R)POST (the reality of postulation) feeds into the subject from below-left via a *dashed* edge to LANG-DY (language dynamics) — conditional. Structural argument: apparent-redefinition-as-concept simultaneously crossed with source-transfer-functionalism and social-reality is mediated by projectional-continuance as central lower hub. The dual-partner formation is the structural claim that European reception of black creative music functioned via two simultaneous partners — source-transfer-functionalism (the cultural transmission mechanism) and social-reality (the lived European condition). The dashed edge between reality-postulation and language-dynamics registers that real postulation has only conditional link to language-dynamics — exposing the diagnostic that European reception expressed real postulation about the music only when the language to articulate that postulation actually obtained. Without language-dynamics, the crossing produces only apparent-redefinition rather than productive source-transfer.
